invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).

Every save control a page offers makes exactly the same checks on that page's answers, with no page an exception: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered still shown, and the controls differ only in where they go once every answer passes (ruling:sam-2026-10-26).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

Data model settled 6 November by ruling:ian-2026-11-06 decisions 4 and 5, so this row's two open questions are closed. A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model: AddressRequest requires at least one role (@NotEmpty) and refuses a type outright (@Null, "type is not a supported field"), and a transporter carries an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status that no address has. It reuses the service's organisation scoping, soft-delete and the Standard Address Block field validation where the fields match. Transporters have no roles — no seventh AddressRole and no fourth RoleGroup — and store the private-or-commercial type instead, which decides the form, the field list and the country rule and so cannot be derived. The address book's own API is unchanged by this row.

increments.detail: Once it is decided that the address book manages transporters, the address book list gains a Transporter tab between 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', headed 'Transporter addresses', with its own columns (Name, Address, Approval number and Type) and a Type filter of 'Commercial' and 'Private', so a trader can see and narrow the organisation's transporters in the same place as its other addresses. It is blocked with the rest of transporter management: nobody has decided whether the service manages transporters at all, or, if it does, whether the address book or something else does.
acceptanceCriteria: The address book list shows a 'Transporter' tab between 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', headed 'Transporter addresses', holding the organisation's addresses of the transporter type (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-022 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-006, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-031; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-088, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-097)
Such an address's Type column reads 'Transporter' on the tabs that show a Type column (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-031)

On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the action column with no visible heading; the address's last line carries the country, an approval number reads in the form 'RO/BUCHAREST/T1/00092010', and Type reads 'Commercial' or 'Private' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-031, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-032 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-035, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-132; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-098)

On the Transporter tab the Type filter offers 'Select one', 'Commercial' and 'Private', and the list it returns holds, across the whole category and filtered on the server, every transporter whose transporter type equals the choice (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-017; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-024; repo:addressbook repo-addressbook-p3-046)
With Welsh selected, the Transporter tab, its heading, its column headings and its Type filter options show their Welsh copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045)

On the address book's transporter tab, the search matches a transporter's approval number as well as its name, town or city and postcode, so entering an approval number finds that transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-020; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-070; repo:addressbook repo-addressbook-p3-032)

sources.ref: repo-addressbook-p3-046 (the list API filters on q and countryCode only, with no type filter)
ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-031 to p2-035, p2-041, p2-043, p2-045 (transporter management blocked; the Transporter tab, its columns and its Welsh wait)

notes: Combines the Transporter tab (req-2040), its columns (req-1135) and its Type filter (req-2041): one tab, one blocker, one set-up. Rewrite of the existing blocked row inc-075, keeping its id. Still blocked: the 26 October ruling says nothing about transporters, so ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm's block stands, and this re-distil only restates the requirements and renumbers the afternoon ruling's claims. Two changes from the existing row's text: its 'Search on the Transporter tab finds a transporter by part of its approval number' criterion is dropped, because no requirement here states it and the search requirement it leaned on (req-1119, held by the address-book split) matches on name, type labels, address lines and country name, not on an approval number; and 'with no Country column' is replaced by naming the four columns and the action column exactly, which proves the same thing positively. Whether a transporter's approval number becomes searchable is for the re-distil after the transporter decision. The category and type query parameter names are the INS service's to choose, so no criterion names one. Waits on the address book split branch's tabs and search rows (externalDependsOn on shared/design-release-2-1/themes/address-book inc-067 and inc-069) and on the add-a-transporter row.

Re-distil 2 November: req-2198 (the search also matches a transporter's approval number) is added here, where the transporter tab's list and search are built, and it waits on the same decision about transporter management. It was given to no area, so the combiner drafted its criterion.

Unblocked 6 November by ruling:ian-2026-11-06: decision 1 makes the address book the system of record, so a Transporter tab has transporter records behind it. Approved transporters are parked (decision 3), so the tab lists the organisation's own transporters only. Open against inc-067, which built three category tabs with a Type column: whether Transporter is a fourth category tab, and how that is worked out from roles now ruling:paul-2026-11-05 has the address book store roles rather than a type. Filtering by private or commercial needs the type on the record, which inc-074's second open question covers.

Settled 6 November by ruling:ian-2026-11-06 decision 5: the Transporter tab is a fourth tab backed by the transporters route, not a fourth role group over the addresses collection. inc-067's three category tabs are role-group views of addresses; this tab is a view of the transporters collection. Filtering by private or commercial reads the type stored on the transporter record (decision 4), so it needs nothing from AddressRole. Note for the plan: a transporter's approval status (Approved or New, shown on the list) is not the address book's AddressStatus, which is an ACTIVE or DELETED soft-delete tombstone — the transporter document needs its own name for its own concept.

Re-analysis 6 November (INS frontend 0f8c051). A concrete blocker for decision 5 the plan must name. The INS front door works an address type out from its roles, as ruling:paul-2026-11-05 requires: services/address-book/address-types.js defines ROLES_BY_ADDRESS_TYPE mapping each of the three ADDRESS_TYPES to its role set, and features/address-book/address-book-tabs.js builds ADDRESS_BOOK_TABS straight off that map, with resolveRole reading from it. So adding TRANSPORTER to ADDRESS_TYPES the obvious way would demand a ROLES_BY_ADDRESS_TYPE[TRANSPORTER] entry, which decision 5 says must not exist. The Transporter type needs its own branch reading the transporters route instead. Say so in the plan, or the first implementor will add a role to make the types line up. One thing comes free: the add flow already uses requiredOneOf('addressType', ...) with a message, so the Transporter radio inherits correct blank-choice validation.

increments.title: Each transporter on the list links to its details page
increments.detail: A trader should be able to check a transporter's full record before choosing it. Once the service holds transporter records with a details page, each row of the transporter list ends with a 'View details' link to that transporter's details page, which brings the trader back to the transporter list they came from. The details page lives where the service holds transporter records, in its own conventions. Blocked: it needs transporter records with a details page, which waits on transporter management being settled.
acceptanceCriteria: Each row of the transporter list ends with a 'View details' link whose visually hidden text names that transporter. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p7-026; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-089, -p8-089-m1)

Following a transporter's 'View details' opens that transporter's details page showing its record, and its Back link returns to the same notification's transporter list. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p8-090, -p9-047; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-106; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-070, -p1-093)

sources.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-070, -p1-093: the details page in the real services' conventions

notes: Blocked by ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-043 (c-285). Kept apart: it needs transporter records with a details page (the address-book rows it depends on) and the reshaped list. The requirement itself says the link is built only once such a details page exists and that until then the list carries no action column, so the row cannot be split into a link now and a page later. c-052 (precedence): the link is adopted, against the parity backlog's claim that it waited.
Unchanged by this re-distil apart from wording.

Unblocked 6 November by ruling:ian-2026-11-06: decision 1 gives a transporter a record in the address book, so there is a details page for the link to open — the address book's own view page (inc-064), reached as inc-066 already returns a viewer to where they opened the address from. The re-distil should check whether this row still needs anything beyond what inc-064 and inc-066 built for addresses, once a transporter is one of them.

Re-analysis 6 November (INS frontend 0f8c051): check before writing anything new. inc-064's address view page and inc-066's return-to-where-it-was-opened-from are both done and merged, so once a transporter is one of the address book's records this row may need little or nothing beyond them. Verify against the built view and delete pages at plan time rather than assuming a new details page is needed.

increments.title: The transporter list refuses a save with no transporter chosen
increments.detail: The data specification makes the transporter mandatory before the trader moves on, so the transporter step cannot be left empty. Today a blank save shows no error and carries on. After this row, either save button on the transporter list holds the trader on the list and names what is missing, and the notification's transporter is only ever set by a real choice. This works over the transporter list as it stands, so it does not wait on how transporters are managed.
acceptanceCriteria: On the transporter list, pressing 'Save and continue' with no transporter chosen keeps the trader on the list and shows 'Select a transporter from the list' in a 'There is a problem' summary that links to the first transporter option, and again inline above the transporter table. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p2-070, -p2-082, -p2-092; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p12-155)

Pressing 'Save and return to overview' with no transporter chosen is refused in the same way: the trader stays on the transporter list with the same summary and the same inline error, and the notification's transporter is left as it was. (ruling:sam-2026-10-26 ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-002, -p1-003, -p1-008, -p1-013)

Choosing a transporter and pressing either button saves it: 'Save and return to overview' goes to the overview, and in both cases the transporter is still chosen when the trader returns to the list. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p12-047; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p18-076; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p11-093)

sources.ref: confluence-6497338582-p2-070, -p2-082, -p2-092: the commercial and the private transporter are mandatory to proceed
ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-002, -p1-003, -p1-008, -p1-013: both save buttons make exactly the same checks, with no page an exception

notes: One slice, req-402. New in this re-distil: it sat in no row before. Not blocked by c-285: the check works over the transporter list as it stands, and the afternoon ruling of 9 October blocks only transporter management, so it is kept apart from the blocked transporter rows and can build now. c-346 (precedence) puts the data specification above the prototype and today's service, both of which let a blank save carry on; the claims c-346 overruled are not relied on anywhere in this row. The message is the copy the service already holds under its required-transporter key in the transport copy folder, so no copy file changes and nothing is invented. The general rule that both save buttons make the same checks on every page (req-1625) is the journey foundation's and builds on its own branch; this row is the transporter list's own instance of it and does not wait for it.
Trimmed 6 November: its navigation (where Save and continue and Back go, the opening run, amend returns) was taken out; EUDPA-774 owns it.

Re-analysis 6 November (animals frontend c31daf4d): still to build, and it is one validator swap. transporters/validate.js already names the right message (copy.errors.transporterRequired, 'Select a transporter from the list') but reaches it through oneOf, which lib/validate/validators.js:189 defines as Joi.string().allow('').valid('', ...values) — so an empty choice passes and the save walks on. requiredOneOf already exists for exactly this (lib/validate/index.js:16, validate.test.js:181, "save-blocking value domain"). Main's own tests state today's behaviour and invert when this lands: transporters.controller.test.js:167 'Should walk on without saving when no transporter is picked' and :210 the same for Save and return to overview.
